title: Signed compatibility declaration for pinned models
creator: Avery Chen
description: We need a machine-readable, signed compatibility declaration that accompanies every pinned model release in the catalog. The declaration must clearly state the input schema (prompt blocks, special tokens), the output shape (JSON/structured outputs, tokenization quirks), parameter semantics (temperature, stop tokens, max_tokens behavior), and the published performance profile (latency p50/p95, throughput for common batch sizes). This ticket defines the contract, the required fields, how declarations are generated and verified, and the minimum verification harness for accepting a pinned model into production.
context: Customers pin model versions to get deterministic behavior for production prompts and SLAs. We continue to see regression risk when upstream models change their tokenization, default decoding behavior, or runtime parameter interpretation. Without a signed contract attached to a pinned version, platform teams and customers lack a single source of truth for what is guaranteed vs best-effort. This causes friction on upgrades and undermines the Dedicated/Private commitments.
proposal: Introduce a signed declaration JSON (compat_declaration_v1) stored in the model catalog alongside model metadata. Declarations include: prompt_schema, output_schema, parameter_contract, tokenizer_checksum, deterministic_signature, perf_profile, and a compatibility_level flag. Declarations are signed by the model-onboarding pipeline (key rotation approved by Security). On onboarding, the runtime runs a verification harness that emits a verification_report artifact; only models with a passing verification_report and valid signature can be listed as pin-eligible in the catalog.
compatibility_level_definitions: strict: no changes allowed to tokenization, reserved tokens, or parameter semantics between minor updates; runtime will reject non-conforming variants.
compatible: allowed non-functional changes (perf improvements, minor formatting) but output shape and parameter semantics must be maintained.
best-effort: best-effort guarantees only; used for experimental or community models.
acceptance_criteria: compat_declaration_v1 schema documented in the onboarding spec and published to Confluence.
Onboarding pipeline outputs signed compat_declaration and verification_report for new pinned models.
Runtime refuses to mark a pinned model as 'pinned' in the catalog without a valid signature and a passing verification_report.
Perf_profile fields p50/p95 latency and throughput at standard batch sizes are present and computed using the standard benchmark harness.
End-to-end integration test that simulates an upgraded model with a changed tokenizer must fail the verification step.
Backward-compat regression alert rule added to Console: if a newly pinned version deviates from the declared output_schema more than X% on canonical prompt set, create a critical incident.
implementation_steps: 1) Define compat_declaration_v1 JSON schema and publish spec.
2) Add signature generation to onboarding pipeline (KMS-backed signing key).
3) Extend verification harness to validate tokenizer checksum, example prompts, and parameter semantics tests.
4) Add runtime catalog validation: require signed declaration for pin eligibility.
5) Add console UI to display declaration and perf_profile next to pinned version entries.
6) Write end-to-end tests and add to CI gating for model onboarding PRs.
tests: integration: onboarding pipeline produces signed declaration and verification_report for a sample model.
regression: harness detects tokenization drift using precomputed tokenizer_checksum.
load: perf_profile runner produces stable p50/p95 numbers within expected variance for reference model on CI machines.
rollout_plan: Week 1: spec review with Runtime, Onboarding, Security, and Console teams.
Week 2: implement schema and signature generation in onboarding pipeline; local verification harness iteration.
Week 3: runtime catalog validation turned on in Dry Run mode (log-only) for 48 hours.
Week 4: enforcement mode ON for new pinned models; retroactively request declarations for top-20 pinned models.
Post rollout: monitor Console alerts and customer support tickets for two weeks; adjust compatibility_level thresholds based on observed false positives.
notes: Decision: we sign declarations from the onboarding pipeline rather than the runtime to ensure CI evidence is included.

Trade-off: strict compatibility_level gives stronger guarantees but increases onboarding friction for minor model fixes; will offer a migration path with canary testing and automated transformation rules.
Follow-up: define a small 'canonical prompt set' per model that onboarding owners must provide for regression detection.
